title: Zingshan Tangkhul Katharuka
subject: Literature
notes: Tangkhul literature textbook for Class VI (Katharuka = Sixth). Catalogued in Bharatavani textbook repository.

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Zingshan Tangkhul Katharuka (Class VI), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (2021). It provides a structured, standardized curriculum from Chapter 1 to the concluding chapter, cultivating mother-tongue literacy, cultural values, grammar mastery, and creative expression for students in Class VI.

chapters.title: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
chapters.summary: Introduction to the ancestral land of Ukhrul, scenic mountains, and community pride.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Zingshan Tangkhul Katharuka wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
chapters.english_translation: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Zingshan Tangkhul Katharuka, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.
grammar_points: Locative marker -li with geographical names: Ukhrul-li, Shirui-li.
Possessive compound: iram (i + ram = our land).
comprehension_questions: Which renowned rare flower blooms on Mount Shirui?
Describe the geographic landscape of Ukhrul in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
chapters.summary: Traditional legends including the tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.
grammar_points: Narrative past tense marked with -yi and -thotna.
Adjectival clause modification of character names.
comprehension_questions: In which historic village did Maitonphi reside?
What moral values does the legend of Shimreishang and Maitonphi convey?

chapters.title: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
chapters.summary: Proverbs transmitting customary ethics, diligence, honor, and community solidarity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
chapters.english_translation: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.
grammar_points: Proverbs commonly use parallel couplet structures.
Comparative suffix -phamei conveys preferential moral superiority.
comprehension_questions: Explain the proverb 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei'.
How do Tangkhul proverbs guide adolescent character formation?

chapters.title: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
chapters.summary: Standard spellings, macron usage, aspirated consonants, and glottal tone marks.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
chapters.english_translation: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).
grammar_points: Minimal vowel length contrasts distinguish lexical meanings.
comprehension_questions: Illustrate three minimal word pairs distinguished by vowel length.
Why is standardized orthography essential for textbooks?

chapters.title: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
chapters.summary: Nouns, pronouns, verbs, case markers (-na, -li, -wui, -eina), and sentence syntax.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
chapters.english_translation: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.
grammar_points: Postpositional clitics attach to noun phrase boundaries.
Verb agreement is aspectual rather than person-concordant.
comprehension_questions: Identify the subject, object, and verb in: 'Mayarnaona lairik pari.'
List the past tense suffixes in modern Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
chapters.summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
chapters.english_translation: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.
grammar_points: Temporal case suffix -tharan indicates 'during / at the time of'.
Cultural compound nouns (Luira Phanit, Haora Kachon).
comprehension_questions: What is the agricultural significance of the Luira festival?
Which traditional shawl is worn during seasonal celebrations?

chapters.title: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
chapters.summary: Classical and modern Tangkhul verses celebrating love, courage, nature, and longing.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,
Zingsho kaphungli leishat laa shakri.
Iram Ukhrul ram wui thot mathamei,
Mayarnaomayana ningkachon pamei.'
Haola tuihi Tangkhul wui akhara shiyan thotna.
chapters.english_translation:
Poetic verse: 'On Phungreitang hill, lovely blossoms unfurl,
Across the eastern ridge, melodies of love arise.
Our Ukhrul homeland generation thrives,
In the hearts of our youth, true devotion endures.'
The Haola poetic genre encapsulates Tangkhul lyricism.
grammar_points: Rhyme and assonance in Tangkhul four-line poetic stanzas.
Repetition of floral and geographical metaphors.
comprehension_questions: What natural imagery is employed in the opening stanza of Meila Won?
Define the oral literary significance of Haola.

chapters.title: Kahaotui: Composition, Writing & Review Exercises
chapters.summary: Practical writing skills, letter composition, paragraph formulation, and chapter reviews.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kapi shiyan: Lairik kapi, shiyan ngashitda chithi kapi. 'Izeishinaoli chithi: Izeinao kaphā, nali khamorwi kahang, ithumwui shimli ungkazip mathalu.' Tuikashak khangachan: Vowels shiyan mashunglu, tuiwon bingli case suffixes sanglu.
chapters.english_translation: Composition exercises: Essay writing and letter composition. 'Letter to a friend: Dear friend, I send you heartfelt greetings and invite you to join us at our home.' Review drills: Verify vowel markings and affix appropriate case suffixes.
grammar_points: Formal salutations in Tangkhul letter writing.
Syntactic coordination of compound sentences using 'kala' (and) and 'kha' (but).
comprehension_questions: Draft a five-sentence letter in Tangkhul inviting a friend to Luira festival.
Complete the grammatical review exercises on nominal cases.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Zingshan Tangkhul Katharuka wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Zingshan Tangkhul Katharuka, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
excerpts.translation_en: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
excerpts.translation_en: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
excerpts.translation_en: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 7: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
excerpts.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,
Zingsho kaphungli leishat laa shakri.
Iram Ukhrul ram wui thot mathamei,
Mayarnaomayana ningkachon pamei.'
Haola tuihi Tangkhul wui akhara shiyan thotna.
excerpts.translation_en:
Poetic verse: 'On Phungreitang hill, lovely blossoms unfurl,
Across the eastern ridge, melodies of love arise.
Our Ukhrul homeland generation thrives,
In the hearts of our youth, true devotion endures.'
The Haola poetic genre encapsulates Tangkhul lyricism.
